actions.label: Project: AI Patient List Podcasts
actions.subtitle: Concise clinical audio updates
actions.previewBody:
AI Patient List Podcasts is a clinician-facing workflow that turns the last 12 hours of patient activity into concise, playable audio briefings. Instead of requiring physicians to scan multiple dashboard views and chart fragments before rounds, the experience packages high-signal events into per-patient podcast items that can be consumed quickly while context-switching between tasks.

The frontend is a Next.js/React application that starts a PromptJob from a physician prompt and then incrementally renders progress as outputs become available. Under the hood, a Flask-based LangChain orchestration layer coordinates tool calls that fetch time-bounded events, draft scripts, synthesize speech, and persist artifacts. Azure Functions provide the typed API boundary for jobs and podcast items, Cosmos DB stores operational and content state, and Azure Blob Storage serves generated audio via secure URLs.

The design emphasizes production reliability as much as generation quality: idempotent job creation, per-patient retries, partial completion visibility, and traceable request IDs across stages. The UI polls job and item endpoints to surface progress without blocking the entire workflow, so one slow patient script does not stall the rest of the list. This makes the system resilient to noisy clinical data, variable generation latency, and transient downstream failures.

From a product perspective, the goal is not novelty for novelty’s sake; it is decision support in a format that matches real clinical pacing. By combining summarization, event filtering, and text-to-speech in a bounded time window, the project explores how AI can reduce cognitive load while preserving relevance, timeliness, and operational transparency.

actions.label: Project: AI-Driven Clinical Copilot
actions.subtitle: Physician-facing RAG copilot for concise, citation-backed clinical summaries and Q&A.
actions.previewBody:
AI Clinical Copilot is a physician-facing workflow built for real clinical pace. Instead of forcing providers to manually sift through fragmented chart history, it assembles patient context into concise, citation-backed answers that can be validated quickly at the point of care.

The frontend is delivered in Next.js/React with a strong emphasis on interaction speed, progressive disclosure, and context retention across follow-up questions. Behind that UI, Python and Azure Functions coordinate retrieval, prompt orchestration, and answer generation over structured and unstructured EHR artifacts.

The core pattern is retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) with explicit grounding: prompts are enriched with relevant chart evidence, response parts are returned with citations, and audit-oriented scoring/guardrail pathways can trigger retries when quality is below threshold. This keeps output useful in practice, not just plausible in a demo.

From a systems perspective, the project combines low-latency UX, typed API contracts, and operational resilience in one loop. The result is a copilot that helps physicians spend less time scrolling and more time deciding, while maintaining the transparency needed for clinical trust.

actions.label: Project: Blackjack
actions.subtitle: Shared rules engine across terminal and WebAssembly clients.
actions.previewBody: Blackjack is a production-style twenty-one implementation where a shared Go rules core powers web and terminal experiences through the same decision logic. The architecture uses a React UI, a postMessage contract boundary, and a Go WASM adapter so state transitions, dealer rules, side-bets, and payouts stay deterministic across clients. Render DTO assembly isolates presentation concerns from domain logic, while diagrammed component, sequence, and state views make behavior traceable for debugging and interviews. It is a practical example of contract-driven integration, state machine modeling, and cross-runtime consistency in a game domain.

actions.label: Project: Patient Assignment List Project
actions.subtitle: Operational assignment control for clinical teams
actions.previewBody: Patient Assignment List is a clinician operations workflow built for high-change environments where ownership, queue visibility, and handoff clarity must stay accurate in real time. Instead of static roster views, it gives teams a manageable assignment surface with drag-and-drop interaction, role-aware filtering, and time-based population criteria designed for shift-driven care. The frontend is implemented with Backbone.js and Handlebars, using AssignmentList and nested VisitList composition so users can move between assignment-level and patient-level context without losing state. Shared pk-common-ui controls keep filtering, paging, and bulk actions consistent while the interaction model remains fast under heavy use. On the backend, Spring MVC and Spring Boot expose versioned REST contracts over facade-driven service boundaries. That separation allows assignment and visit DTO contracts to remain stable while business rules, mappers, and DAO queries evolve behind the facade layer, reducing UI churn and making incremental backend changes safer. The implementation emphasizes reliability and predictability: debounced query flows, server-side pagination and filter semantics, authorization checks scoped to assignment context, and observability telemetry around assignee changes, filter behavior, and query latency. The result is a workflow that helps clinical teams rebalance patient ownership quickly while preserving trust in system state.

actions.label: Project: Patient List Project
actions.subtitle: Configurable visit intelligence at point of care
actions.previewBody: Patient List is a physician-facing workflow designed for high-volume clinical rounding, where speed and precision matter more than ornamental UI. Instead of forcing providers to scan scattered views, it consolidates visit context into a configurable list surface with reliable filtering, sorting, and pagination tuned for real-world throughput. Shared pk-common-ui components provide consistent controls for search, filters, and table interactions so the experience remains predictable even as requirements evolve. On the backend, Spring Web MVC and Spring Boot expose versioned REST endpoints backed by a facade-oriented service layer. That separation lets DTO contracts stay stable while domain and DAO logic can evolve independently, reducing churn in the UI and enabling incremental backend improvements without breaking physician workflows. The system is engineered for operational reliability as much as usability: server-side query optimization, robust pagination semantics, authorization checks at service boundaries, and observability telemetry around route/filter activity and query latency. The result is a patient-list application that helps clinicians find the right patients and act faster, while preserving trust in both data quality and response behavior.

actions.label: Technology: Axios
actions.subtitle: AI-Driven Clinical Copilot
actions.previewBody: Used in AI-Driven Clinical Copilot.
keywords:
AI Clinical Copilot is a physician-facing workflow built for real clinical pace. Instead of forcing providers to manually sift through fragmented chart history, it assembles patient context into concise, citation-backed answers that can be validated quickly at the point of care.

The frontend is delivered in Next.js/React with a strong emphasis on interaction speed, progressive disclosure, and context retention across follow-up questions. Behind that UI, Python and Azure Functions coordinate retrieval, prompt orchestration, and answer generation over structured and unstructured EHR artifacts.

The core pattern is retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) with explicit grounding: prompts are enriched with relevant chart evidence, response parts are returned with citations, and audit-oriented scoring/guardrail pathways can trigger retries when quality is below threshold. This keeps output useful in practice, not just plausible in a demo.

From a systems perspective, the project combines low-latency UX, typed API contracts, and operational resilience in one loop. The result is a copilot that helps physicians spend less time scrolling and more time deciding, while maintaining the transparency needed for clinical trust.

actions.label: Technology: Azure Blob Storage
actions.subtitle: AI Patient List Podcasts
actions.previewTitle: Azure Blob Storage • AI Patient List Podcasts
actions.previewBody: Used in AI Patient List Podcasts.
keywords:
AI Patient List Podcasts is a clinician-facing workflow that turns the last 12 hours of patient activity into concise, playable audio briefings. Instead of requiring physicians to scan multiple dashboard views and chart fragments before rounds, the experience packages high-signal events into per-patient podcast items that can be consumed quickly while context-switching between tasks.

The frontend is a Next.js/React application that starts a PromptJob from a physician prompt and then incrementally renders progress as outputs become available. Under the hood, a Flask-based LangChain orchestration layer coordinates tool calls that fetch time-bounded events, draft scripts, synthesize speech, and persist artifacts. Azure Functions provide the typed API boundary for jobs and podcast items, Cosmos DB stores operational and content state, and Azure Blob Storage serves generated audio via secure URLs.

The design emphasizes production reliability as much as generation quality: idempotent job creation, per-patient retries, partial completion visibility, and traceable request IDs across stages. The UI polls job and item endpoints to surface progress without blocking the entire workflow, so one slow patient script does not stall the rest of the list. This makes the system resilient to noisy clinical data, variable generation latency, and transient downstream failures.

From a product perspective, the goal is not novelty for novelty’s sake; it is decision support in a format that matches real clinical pacing. By combining summarization, event filtering, and text-to-speech in a bounded time window, the project explores how AI can reduce cognitive load while preserving relevance, timeliness, and operational transparency.

actions.label: Technology: Backbone.js
actions.subtitle: Patient List Project
actions.previewBody: Used in Patient List Project.
keywords: Patient List is a physician-facing workflow designed for high-volume clinical rounding, where speed and precision matter more than ornamental UI. Instead of forcing providers to scan scattered views, it consolidates visit context into a configurable list surface with reliable filtering, sorting, and pagination tuned for real-world throughput. The frontend uses Backbone.js and Handlebars with a router-driven state model that keeps list criteria, paging, and sort behavior stable as clinicians move through workflows. Shared pk-common-ui components provide consistent controls for search, filters, and table interactions so the experience remains predictable even as requirements evolve. On the backend, Spring Web MVC and Spring Boot expose versioned REST endpoints backed by a facade-oriented service layer. That separation lets DTO contracts stay stable while domain and DAO logic can evolve independently, reducing churn in the UI and enabling incremental backend improvements without breaking physician workflows. The system is engineered for operational reliability as much as usability: server-side query optimization, robust pagination semantics, authorization checks at service boundaries, and observability telemetry around route/filter activity and query latency. The result is a patient-list application that helps clinicians find the right patients and act faster, while preserving trust in both data quality and response behavior.

actions.label: Technology: Backbone.js
actions.subtitle: Patient Assignment List Project
actions.previewBody: Used in Patient Assignment List Project.
keywords: Patient Assignment List is a clinician operations workflow built for high-change environments where ownership, queue visibility, and handoff clarity must stay accurate in real time. Instead of static roster views, it gives teams a manageable assignment surface with drag-and-drop interaction, role-aware filtering, and time-based population criteria designed for shift-driven care. The frontend is implemented with Backbone.js and Handlebars, using AssignmentList and nested VisitList composition so users can move between assignment-level and patient-level context without losing state. Shared pk-common-ui controls keep filtering, paging, and bulk actions consistent while the interaction model remains fast under heavy use. On the backend, Spring MVC and Spring Boot expose versioned REST contracts over facade-driven service boundaries. That separation allows assignment and visit DTO contracts to remain stable while business rules, mappers, and DAO queries evolve behind the facade layer, reducing UI churn and making incremental backend changes safer. The implementation emphasizes reliability and predictability: debounced query flows, server-side pagination and filter semantics, authorization checks scoped to assignment context, and observability telemetry around assignee changes, filter behavior, and query latency. The result is a workflow that helps clinical teams rebalance patient ownership quickly while preserving trust in system state.

AI Clinical Copilot is a physician-facing workflow built for real clinical pace. Instead of forcing providers to manually sift through fragmented chart history, it assembles patient context into concise, citation-backed answers that can be validated quickly at the point of care.

The frontend is delivered in Next.js/React with a strong emphasis on interaction speed, progressive disclosure, and context retention across follow-up questions. Behind that UI, Python and Azure Functions coordinate retrieval, prompt orchestration, and answer generation over structured and unstructured EHR artifacts.

The core pattern is retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) with explicit grounding: prompts are enriched with relevant chart evidence, response parts are returned with citations, and audit-oriented scoring/guardrail pathways can trigger retries when quality is below threshold. This keeps output useful in practice, not just plausible in a demo.

From a systems perspective, the project combines low-latency UX, typed API contracts, and operational resilience in one loop. The result is a copilot that helps physicians spend less time scrolling and more time deciding, while maintaining the transparency needed for clinical trust.

keywords: Patient List is a physician-facing workflow designed for high-volume clinical rounding, where speed and precision matter more than ornamental UI. Instead of forcing providers to scan scattered views, it consolidates visit context into a configurable list surface with reliable filtering, sorting, and pagination tuned for real-world throughput. The frontend uses Backbone.js and Handlebars with a router-driven state model that keeps list criteria, paging, and sort behavior stable as clinicians move through workflows. Shared pk-common-ui components provide consistent controls for search, filters, and table interactions so the experience remains predictable even as requirements evolve. On the backend, Spring Web MVC and Spring Boot expose versioned REST endpoints backed by a facade-oriented service layer. That separation lets DTO contracts stay stable while domain and DAO logic can evolve independently, reducing churn in the UI and enabling incremental backend improvements without breaking physician workflows. The system is engineered for operational reliability as much as usability: server-side query optimization, robust pagination semantics, authorization checks at service boundaries, and observability telemetry around route/filter activity and query latency. The result is a patient-list application that helps clinicians find the right patients and act faster, while preserving trust in both data quality and response behavior.

keywords: Patient Assignment List is a clinician operations workflow built for high-change environments where ownership, queue visibility, and handoff clarity must stay accurate in real time. Instead of static roster views, it gives teams a manageable assignment surface with drag-and-drop interaction, role-aware filtering, and time-based population criteria designed for shift-driven care. The frontend is implemented with Backbone.js and Handlebars, using AssignmentList and nested VisitList composition so users can move between assignment-level and patient-level context without losing state. Shared pk-common-ui controls keep filtering, paging, and bulk actions consistent while the interaction model remains fast under heavy use. On the backend, Spring MVC and Spring Boot expose versioned REST contracts over facade-driven service boundaries. That separation allows assignment and visit DTO contracts to remain stable while business rules, mappers, and DAO queries evolve behind the facade layer, reducing UI churn and making incremental backend changes safer. The implementation emphasizes reliability and predictability: debounced query flows, server-side pagination and filter semantics, authorization checks scoped to assignment context, and observability telemetry around assignee changes, filter behavior, and query latency. The result is a workflow that helps clinical teams rebalance patient ownership quickly while preserving trust in system state.

keywords:
AI Patient List Podcasts is a clinician-facing workflow that turns the last 12 hours of patient activity into concise, playable audio briefings. Instead of requiring physicians to scan multiple dashboard views and chart fragments before rounds, the experience packages high-signal events into per-patient podcast items that can be consumed quickly while context-switching between tasks.

The frontend is a Next.js/React application that starts a PromptJob from a physician prompt and then incrementally renders progress as outputs become available. Under the hood, a Flask-based LangChain orchestration layer coordinates tool calls that fetch time-bounded events, draft scripts, synthesize speech, and persist artifacts. Azure Functions provide the typed API boundary for jobs and podcast items, Cosmos DB stores operational and content state, and Azure Blob Storage serves generated audio via secure URLs.

The design emphasizes production reliability as much as generation quality: idempotent job creation, per-patient retries, partial completion visibility, and traceable request IDs across stages. The UI polls job and item endpoints to surface progress without blocking the entire workflow, so one slow patient script does not stall the rest of the list. This makes the system resilient to noisy clinical data, variable generation latency, and transient downstream failures.

From a product perspective, the goal is not novelty for novelty’s sake; it is decision support in a format that matches real clinical pacing. By combining summarization, event filtering, and text-to-speech in a bounded time window, the project explores how AI can reduce cognitive load while preserving relevance, timeliness, and operational transparency.
